html:
The giant collective units that organised rural China from 1958 to the early 1980s. Each commune merged many villages, often thousands of households, and ran farming, small industry, schools, militia and local government together.

They were launched in 1958 as part of Mao Zedong's Great Leap Forward. Private plots were taken, and in many places families ate in communal canteens. Officials under pressure reported impossible harvests, and the state took grain on those false figures, while peasants were pulled off the fields to make steel in backyard furnaces. The result was the Great Chinese Famine of 1959 to 1961, in which tens of millions died.

The communes were later scaled back but lasted until Deng Xiaoping's reforms. The household responsibility system let families farm their own plots again, output rose fast, and the communes were wound up in the mid 1980s. Compare Soviet collectivisation, which also ended in famine.
sum: The giant collective units that organised rural China from 1958 to the early 1980s. Each commune merged many villages, often thousands of households, and ran farming, small industry, schools, militia and local government together.
